title: What Was the Loudest Natural Sound Ever Recorded?
description:
People thousands of kilometres away heard the 1883 Krakatoa eruption.

The 1883 Krakatoa eruption is often described as the loudest sound in recorded history.

The eruption generated enormous pressure waves that travelled around the globe multiple times; historical accounts and barometers documented them.

The sound was heard roughly 4,800 km away, though exact “loudest” rankings depend on reconstruction and measurement.
